The paper constructs anytime-valid inference for sequential forecaster comparison by embedding the score differential process into a game-theoretic supermartingale framework. Let X_t = S(Y_t, f_t^1) − S(Y_t, f_t^2) be the bounded score difference at time t. The empirical Bernstein CS uses the self-normalized sum: Δ̂_t ± √(2V̂_t log(2/α)/t) + 3log(2/α)/t, derived from a method-of-mixtures boundary on the exponential supermartingale exp(λ∑X_i − ψ(λ)t). Ville's inequality ℙ(∃t: M_t ≥ 1/α) ≤ α converts the supermartingale M_t = ∏(1+λ_i X_i) into a uniform boundary. The e-process E_t = ∏ dℚ/dℙ(X_i) tests the weak null 𝔼[Δ_t] ≤ 0 by measuring evidence against ℙ. Duality: CS inversion yields sequential tests; e-process integration yields CS. Failure modes: (1) unbounded scores break sub-exponential assumption, requiring truncation; (2) non-stationary variance inflates V̂_t causing over-coverage; (3) adversarial forecaster correlation violates conditional independence, invalidating supermartingale property.
